title: Morning Edition
notes: It prioritizes developments since Sunday’s morning edition: China’s confirmation of Thursday’s Xi–Trump–Putin summit in Shenzhen, the failure of ULA’s Vulcan rocket with 40 Amazon satellites, the Edmonton Elks’ Grey Cup win, New World Development’s rights issue and share plunge, and the Yemeni government forces’ retreat toward Aden.

Ongoing stories — the U.S. flight disruptions after the Nov. 13 ground stop and the New Orleans river collision — carry their original and updated dates. Hong Kong’s police facial-recognition rollout, covered in Sunday’s edition, is not repeated.

Items described as planned or scheduled — the Shenzhen summit and APEC meetings, the Grammy nominations announcement, Voyager 1’s light-day milestone and Haiti’s July election — are not presented as having happened. The Grammy nominees had not been announced when this edition was prepared.

This edition has photos on the lead and on 18 of 22 other stories, using only Wikimedia Commons or U.S. government public-domain files, each credited. All are file photos or illustrations that do not show the events described. The Shenzhen security, Grammy, Toronto Tempo and John Lee APEC stories are text-only because no suitable free photo was found.

Stories by region: U.S. 5, Canada 5, Hong Kong 5, China 3, World 5. China has three: most China news this morning centred on the Shenzhen summit and APEC week, which these stories cover, and no further story met the bar for this edition.
provenance: Stories are compiled from the linked sources; labels describe the type of claim each story rests on.
Source pages were opened during this morning’s research between about 6:19 and 6:27 AM ET; each check time is the logged time that page was fetched.

RTHK is Hong Kong’s government-funded public broadcaster; info.gov.hk pages and SAnews are government releases; Grammy.com is the Recording Academy’s own site. Some RTHK and HKFP items are Reuters or AFP wire copy and are marked as such.

A France 24 page on the Yemen retreat returned an access error (HTTP 403) to the automated fetch and a Bangkok Post page returned no readable text; these are access limits, not evidence that the reporting is wrong, and they are not cited.
Where outlets gave different figures — U.S. flight cancellations and injuries in the Phuket fire — the edition states each and who reported it.

stories.headline: U.S. flights expected back near full capacity on Monday after the weekend’s ground-stop chaos, Duffy says
stories.deck: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Sunday that U.S. air travel should be running at full capacity by Monday, and American Airlines said it planned a largely normal schedule, after Friday’s nationwide ground stop disrupted flights all weekend.
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Sunday that U.S. air travel should be running at full capacity by Monday, and American Airlines said it planned a largely normal schedule, after Friday’s nationwide ground stop disrupted flights all weekend. Duffy said planes and crews were “out of position” after the stop of more than four hours, which the BBC described as the longest nationwide grounding since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. Counts of the damage differ by source and time: the BBC cited Bloomberg, quoting aviation data firms, as saying cancellations had topped 17,000 by Sunday, while NPR cited FlightAware figures of more than 2,300 cancellations and more than 8,000 delays on Sunday evening alone. Duffy has blamed work by contractor L3Harris replacing old copper wiring with fibre-optic cable, which he said overloaded the FAA’s legacy equipment; L3Harris said it takes the incident seriously.
stories.why: Travellers should still expect knock-on delays as airlines reposition crews and planes. The bigger question — how a routine upgrade could halt every U.S. flight — goes to the age of the air-traffic system and will shape the debate over funding its replacement.
stories.label: Reported + Official statement

stories.headline: ULA’s Vulcan rocket fails 10 minutes after launch, destroying 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites
stories.deck: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after lifting off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, losing all 40 satellites it was carrying for Amazon’s Leo broadband network in the company’s first outright mission failure.
stories.summary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after lifting off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, losing all 40 satellites it was carrying for Amazon’s Leo broadband network in the company’s first outright mission failure. ULA, a Boeing–Lockheed Martin joint venture formed in 2006, said the vehicle “suffered an anomaly” and that it did not yet have data on the cause. Ars Technica, citing unnamed sources, reported that the problem occurred in the booster stage rather than the upper stage or strap-on boosters. It was Vulcan’s fifth flight and its first in about nine months, after separate investigations into its solid rocket boosters and its BE-4 main engines, and the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has booked for its planned constellation of more than 3,200 satellites. The failure is expected to ground the rocket, which also carries about half of the U.S. military’s national-security launches in the coming years, Ars reported.
stories.why: Amazon is racing SpaceX’s Starlink, and its main launch provider is now grounded for an unknown period. With the Pentagon also relying on Vulcan, the loss deepens U.S. dependence on SpaceX at a time when competition in launch was supposed to be growing.
stories.label: Reported + Official statement + Unnamed sources

stories.headline: NTSB says the tanker that hit a docked New Orleans riverboat had a steering failure that left its rudder stuck
stories.deck: Federal investigators said on Sunday that the tanker Atlantic Asphalt suffered a “steering casualty” that kept its rudder turned to starboard before it struck the docked riverboat American Heritage on the Mississippi on Friday.
stories.summary: Federal investigators said on Sunday that the tanker Atlantic Asphalt suffered a “steering casualty” that kept its rudder turned to starboard before it struck the docked riverboat American Heritage on the Mississippi on Friday. The exact cause of the steering problem has not been determined, investigator-in-charge Bart Barnum said, adding that the voyage data recorder captured a warning signal and orders to drop anchor and take emergency action minutes before the crash. The American Heritage, carrying 140 passengers and 50 crew, capsized within 22 minutes, ABC News reported, citing the NTSB; more than 30 people were injured and all aboard were accounted for. A preliminary NTSB report is expected in about 30 days. The Port of New Orleans has separately sued the tanker’s owners.
stories.why: A steering failure points investigators toward the tanker’s equipment and maintenance rather than the docked riverboat, which will shape liability in the lawsuits already filed. It also raises questions about safety margins for passenger vessels moored along a busy commercial river.

stories.headline: Voyager 1 is set to become the first spacecraft one light-day from Earth on Wednesday, and NASA wants the world to flash it a message
stories.deck: NASA says Voyager 1, launched in 1977, will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth — about 16 billion miles — at 5:16:07 a.m. EST on Wednesday, Nov. 18, and is inviting people to flash its call sign at the sky on Tuesday night.
stories.summary: NASA says Voyager 1, launched in 1977, will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth — about 16 billion miles — at 5:16:07 a.m. EST on Wednesday, Nov. 18, and is inviting people to flash its call sign at the sky on Tuesday night. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, so a command sent to the probe will take a day to arrive and another day for a reply to return. For “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day,” NASA is asking people to blink “VGR” in Morse code with phones or flashlights after sunset on Nov. 17. Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn, became the most distant human-made object in 1998 and entered interstellar space in 2012. NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory plans a public discussion with mission members on Nov. 19.
stories.why: A nearly 50-year-old spacecraft still sending data from interstellar space is one of engineering’s great endurance stories, and the milestone is an easy invitation for anyone to take part — no telescope required.
stories.label: Official statement + Reported

stories.headline: Grammy nominations are set to be announced Monday morning, with five new categories including best Asian pop music performance
stories.deck: Nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards are scheduled to be revealed in a livestream starting at 7:45 a.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 16, with the full list due on Grammy.com at 9 a.m. ET.
stories.summary: Nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards are scheduled to be revealed in a livestream starting at 7:45 a.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 16, with the full list due on Grammy.com at 9 a.m. ET. Presenters named by the Recording Academy include Herbie Hancock, Pharrell Williams, Olivia Dean, Renée Fleming, Kehlani and Yungblud. This year’s awards add five categories: best Latin song, best traditional folk album, best traditional pop vocal performance, best R&B collaboration or duo/group performance, and best Asian pop music performance — the last of which drew criticism from some K-pop fans and artists, CBC reported. Artists can now enter best new artist up to four times in their careers instead of three. The ceremony is scheduled for Feb. 7, 2027.
stories.why: The nominations set the music industry’s awards season and often shape streaming and touring for months. The new Asian pop category is a test of whether the Grammys can recognise K-pop’s global reach without, as critics fear, walling it off from the main awards.
stories.label: Official statement + Reported

stories.headline: Edmonton Elks beat the Montreal Alouettes 37-30 to win the 113th Grey Cup, after the Snowbirds’ last Tutor flypast
stories.deck: Quarterback Cody Fajardo threw two touchdown passes and ran for two more as the Edmonton Elks beat the Montreal Alouettes 37-30 in Calgary on Sunday for their first Grey Cup since 2015.
stories.summary: Quarterback Cody Fajardo threw two touchdown passes and ran for two more as the Edmonton Elks beat the Montreal Alouettes 37-30 in Calgary on Sunday for their first Grey Cup since 2015. Fajardo, named the game’s most valuable player, won against the team he led to the 2023 title before being traded to Edmonton. Vincent Blanchard’s late field goals sealed it after Montreal turned the ball over on downs with 1:40 left. The Elks finished last in the West Division a season ago; it is their 15th championship. Montreal, the CFL’s best regular-season team at 14-4, lost a second straight Grey Cup. Before kickoff, the Canadian Forces Snowbirds flew over McMahon Stadium in their final public flight in the CT-114 Tutor jets the team has flown since it was formed. “Thank you Canada, for 55 years of support,” team lead Maj. Maciej Hatta said.
stories.why: Edmonton’s turnaround from last place to champion in a year is the kind of story that keeps the CFL relevant, and Fajardo’s win over his old team gives it extra bite. The Snowbirds’ farewell marks the end of an aircraft generations of Canadians grew up watching.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: Russia will not play at next month’s world junior hockey championship in Alberta, citing Canada’s entry restrictions
stories.deck: The International Ice Hockey Federation said on Sunday that Russia cannot take part in the world junior championship in Edmonton and Red Deer because of restrictions set by the Canadian government, despite a sports-court ruling ordering its return.
stories.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation said on Sunday that Russia cannot take part in the world junior championship in Edmonton and Red Deer because of restrictions set by the Canadian government, despite a sports-court ruling ordering its return. The IIHF said Canada will remain host and the under-20 tournament will run from Dec. 26 to Jan. 5. The Court of Arbitration for Sport had ruled last month that Russia must be allowed back into IIHF events, from which it has been suspended since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the decision “unacceptable” and “unlawful” and politically motivated, and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee.
stories.why: Ottawa has effectively overridden a sports-court ruling by refusing entry, setting up a fight over who decides when Russia returns to international sport. Expect the dispute to follow the IIHF to the IOC and future host countries.
stories.label: Official statement + Reported

stories.headline: Carney says Canada could turn to European, Japanese or Chinese automakers if U.S. trade talks fail its auto sector
stories.deck: Prime Minister Mark Carney said in Cambodia that negotiations with Washington remain his priority, but if they fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry, Canada will look at “European options, Asian options.”
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said in Cambodia that negotiations with Washington remain his priority, but if they fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry, Canada will look at “European options, Asian options.” Speaking at the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh, Carney said the market had become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions, as Washington threatens tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian autos by January, Global News reported. Asked whether potential Chinese investment was leverage, he told reporters: “It’s not leverage. But action, reaction,” according to the Guardian, which said he mentioned Chinese and Japanese automakers among the alternatives. Carney is expected to meet Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week; in January the two governments agreed to let up to 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at a 6.1% tariff.
stories.why: Carney is signalling to Washington that Canada’s auto plants have other suitors, without walking away from the table. Any move toward Chinese carmakers would test ties with the U.S. — and is worth watching at his expected meeting with Xi this week.
stories.label: Official statement + Reported

stories.headline: Three 24-year-old friends finish an 8,000-km canoe trip across Canada at Vancouver’s Jericho Beach
stories.deck: Nolan Aziz, Will Vyse and Georges Kirijian, all 24 and from Toronto, paddled ashore at Jericho Beach on Sunday after 219 days and about 8,000 kilometres from Tadoussac, Quebec, raising money for remote northern Indigenous communities.
stories.summary: Nolan Aziz, Will Vyse and Georges Kirijian, all 24 and from Toronto, paddled ashore at Jericho Beach on Sunday after 219 days and about 8,000 kilometres from Tadoussac, Quebec, raising money for remote northern Indigenous communities. The trio set out in April and travelled through six provinces on rivers and lakes, often far from cities, CBC News reported. Family, friends and supporters cheered and sang O Canada as they stepped ashore. The friends believe theirs is the longest single-season canoe expedition on record, a claim CBC attributed to them.
stories.why: A small, cheerful story of endurance across the country — and a reminder of how much of Canada is still best reached by water.

stories.headline: New World Development shares plunge more than 45% after it proposes a HK$24.9 billion rights issue
stories.deck: Shares of New World Development fell more than 45% at Monday’s open to HK$2.655, an all-time low since its 1980 listing, after the heavily indebted developer proposed raising about HK$24.9 billion through a deeply discounted rights issue.
stories.summary: Shares of New World Development fell more than 45% at Monday’s open to HK$2.655, an all-time low since its 1980 listing, after the heavily indebted developer proposed raising about HK$24.9 billion through a deeply discounted rights issue. The plan offers 11 new shares for every share held at HK$0.90 each, 81.5% below Friday’s close of HK$4.87, according to a company filing reported by RTHK. About a third of the proceeds would prepay 10% of roughly HK$82 billion in bank loans, with the rest of those loans extended by two years, and another third would repay other debt. Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises, which owns about 45.3%, has committed to take up its full entitlement, and the rest is underwritten. JP Morgan said the discount was likely beyond most investors’ expectations and that the money would ease, but not end, the company’s liquidity stress.
stories.why: New World is one of Hong Kong’s best-known developers, and asking shareholders for more than three times its remaining market value shows how deep the property slump has cut. Its fate is a bellwether for lenders and other developers in the city.

stories.summary: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing launched the HKEX Offshore RMB Bond Index on Monday, developed with Bloomberg, its stock exchange’s first bond index. Financial Secretary Paul Chan said at the launch that the index, which tracks more than 300 renminbi bonds listed in the city, gives investors a clear benchmark and lays the foundation for index-linked products such as funds and exchange-traded funds. “Like a landmark on a city’s skyline, a good index gives a market a recognisable point of reference,” he said, arguing that broader participation could lower trading and funding costs.
stories.why: Beijing wants more of the world to borrow and invest in yuan, and Hong Kong is its main offshore testing ground. An index is a modest technical step, but it is the kind of plumbing that makes it easier for global funds to buy in.

stories.headline: John Lee calls Hong Kong a “port in a storm” for shipowners as Maritime Week opens
stories.deck: Chief Executive John Lee told the opening of Hong Kong Maritime Week on Monday that the city is a “safe harbour” for international shipping amid geopolitical upheaval and that it “firmly rejects isolationism.”
stories.summary: Chief Executive John Lee told the opening of Hong Kong Maritime Week on Monday that the city is a “safe harbour” for international shipping amid geopolitical upheaval and that it “firmly rejects isolationism.” Lee said the city hosts around 1,200 port and maritime-related companies, warned that “protectionism and fragmentation threaten the global economy,” and said the future of maritime trade depends on keeping shipping lanes open and upholding international maritime law. The government said it is steering Hong Kong from a regional port into a global maritime hub focused on high-value services, and Lee said a task force is developing a green-fuel trading platform for shipping.

stories.headline: Hundreds pray for the Tai Po fire victims at a Catholic mass after police questioned the church about it
stories.deck: Hundreds of people, including former Wang Fuk Court residents, packed the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church in Tai Po on Sunday evening for a mass remembering the 168 people killed in last November’s fire, Hong Kong Free Press reported.
stories.summary: Hundreds of people, including former Wang Fuk Court residents, packed the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church in Tai Po on Sunday evening for a mass remembering the 168 people killed in last November’s fire, Hong Kong Free Press reported. Cardinal Stephen Chow later asked parishes to hold special masses for the first anniversary. Auxiliary Bishop Joseph Ha, who gave individual blessings to former residents, acknowledged police had approached the church, calling it “a misunderstanding” and “normal stuff.” Some worshippers questioned why police were involved.
stories.why: As the first anniversary approaches, how and whether residents can mourn publicly has become a sensitive question in Hong Kong. The church’s careful wording, and the bishop’s low-key answer, show how cautiously even religious groups now move.

stories.headline: China confirms Xi will host the first-ever summit with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday
stories.deck: China’s foreign ministry said on Monday that Xi Jinping will hold a China‑Russia‑US heads‑of‑state meeting with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Nov. 19, the first face‑to‑face meeting of the three countries’ leaders. Trump is due in Manila for the ASEAN summit first.
stories.summary: China’s foreign ministry said on Monday that Xi Jinping will hold a China‑Russia‑US heads‑of‑state meeting with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Nov. 19, the first face‑to‑face meeting of the three countries’ leaders. Trump is due in Manila for the ASEAN summit first. Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the leaders would “exchange in-depth views on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability,” calling the meeting of “groundbreaking significance,” RTHK reported. The White House and the Kremlin had already confirmed the three-way meeting, which is planned on the sidelines of the APEC leaders’ gathering in the city. Trump wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and the Iran war, but U.S. officials said Russia’s war in Ukraine is not expected to be on his agenda, according to AFP via Hong Kong Free Press. A White House official told NPR that no agreement on denuclearization is expected and called the meeting an “entry point”; China has long said the U.S. and Russia should cut their own arsenals before it joins such talks. Trump stops first in Manila for the ASEAN summit, where the Guardian says he is expected to sign a trade agreement with Thailand; NPR reports that Elon Musk is joining him in Shenzhen. It is Trump’s first overseas trip since his party’s heavy losses in this month’s midterm elections.
stories.why: A three-way meeting of the U.S., Chinese and Russian leaders has never happened before, and the setting lets Xi play host to both. Expectations of concrete deals are low, so the signals that come out — on nuclear arms, Iran, trade and whether Ukraine is raised at all — will matter more than any communiqué.
stories.label: Official statement + Reported
stories.note: The summit is scheduled; nothing in this story describes it as having taken place.

stories.headline: China’s October retail sales, factory output and investment all miss forecasts
stories.deck: Official data released on Monday showed retail sales up just 0.4% from a year earlier in October and industrial output up 4.8%, both below economists’ estimates, while fixed-asset investment shrank 8.1% in the first ten months.
stories.summary: Official data released on Monday showed retail sales up just 0.4% from a year earlier in October and industrial output up 4.8%, both below economists’ estimates, while fixed-asset investment shrank 8.1% in the first ten months. Analysts had expected retail sales to rise 0.8% and output 5.3%, CNBC reported; retail sales growth slowed from 1.1% in September and output from 5.5%. CNBC said the investment decline, which includes property and infrastructure, was worse than the 7% fall analysts had expected. The National Bureau of Statistics highlighted that industrial output rose 5.3% over the first ten months, with high-end and intelligent manufacturing contributing more than half, and RTHK noted strong demand for AI-related products and cars and that October exports had surged. Third-quarter growth was 4.5% year on year.
stories.why: Weak shoppers and shrinking investment, set against booming high-tech exports, show an economy leaning on foreign demand. That gives Beijing more at stake in this week’s APEC and Trump–Xi diplomacy, and more reason to consider support for consumers.

stories.headline: Fire at a motorcycle rental shop in Phuket’s Patong kills 11 people, mostly from smoke
stories.deck: A pre-dawn fire that started at a motorcycle rental business in Patong, on Thailand’s resort island of Phuket, killed 11 people on Monday and spread through neighbouring shophouses, police said.
stories.summary: A pre-dawn fire that started at a motorcycle rental business in Patong, on Thailand’s resort island of Phuket, killed 11 people on Monday and spread through neighbouring shophouses, police said. The blaze was reported at about 3:17 a.m. local time; officials said about 100 motorcycles, fuel, oil, tyres and plastics fed thick, toxic smoke that trapped people living on the upper floors, and most of the dead are believed to have died from smoke inhalation. Police said an initial investigation pointed to an exploding electrical transformer or a short circuit on a utility pole, and ruled out arson. Injury counts differ: Al Jazeera, citing police, reported 16; the Phuket News, citing a later police update, 18; the Nation reported 36 taken to hospital. Authorities said no tourists were among the dead or injured, according to Al Jazeera.
stories.why: Patong is one of Asia’s busiest tourist strips, and the deaths of workers living above a shop full of fuel and motorcycles point to a familiar problem: mixed-use buildings with weak fire separation. Expect pressure on Thai authorities over inspections, months after another deadly fire.
stories.label: Reported + Official statement

stories.headline: Seventeen people are shot dead in two unrelated mass shootings in South Africa
stories.deck: South African police are investigating the killings of 17 people in two separate shootings on Sunday night, one outside Pietermaritzburg in KwaZulu-Natal and one in a shack west of Pretoria.
stories.summary: South African police are investigating the killings of 17 people in two separate shootings on Sunday night, one outside Pietermaritzburg in KwaZulu-Natal and one in a shack west of Pretoria. Police said eight men were found with multiple gunshot wounds inside a bullet-riddled seven-seater vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg. In the Jeffsville informal settlement in Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, the bodies of six men and three women were found in a four-room shack; they are believed to have been killed between 10 and 11 p.m. Police say the incidents are unrelated, motives have not been established, and no arrests had been reported.
stories.why: South Africa has one of the world’s highest murder rates, and mass shootings like these keep crime at the top of voters’ concerns. Whether police can quickly find suspects in either case will be watched as a test of the state’s capacity.

stories.deck: Yemen’s Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces said on Sunday they were withdrawing from Dhubab and the area overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait to reinforce the interim capital, Aden, ending a weeks-long counter-offensive against the Iran-backed Houthis.
stories.summary: Yemen’s Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces said on Sunday they were withdrawing from Dhubab and the area overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait to reinforce the interim capital, Aden, ending a weeks-long counter-offensive against the Iran-backed Houthis. The force said securing Aden and neighbouring provinces was the “priority.” Houthi-run media said the movement had taken control of the evacuated territory; Saudi Arabia had not commented, the BBC reported. Government and military sources told AFP, as cited by DW, that Houthi forces were about 60 kilometres from Aden. The Houthis seized much of the coast near the strait, at the southern mouth of the Red Sea, in a September offensive.
stories.why: Bab al-Mandab is one of the world’s busiest shipping chokepoints, so Houthi control of its shore threatens trade between Asia and Europe. A Houthi push on Aden would also put the internationally recognised government’s last major base at risk.

stories.headline: Martine Moïse, widow of Haiti’s assassinated president, registers to run in the first presidential election in a decade
stories.deck: Martine Moïse, who was wounded in the 2021 attack that killed her husband, President Jovenel Moïse, appeared on Sunday on the electoral council’s list of 33 registered presidential candidates.
stories.summary: Martine Moïse, who was wounded in the 2021 attack that killed her husband, President Jovenel Moïse, appeared on Sunday on the electoral council’s list of 33 registered presidential candidates. Other registered candidates include former presidents Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert and former prime minister Claude Joseph. Haiti last held a presidential election in 2016; elections planned for December were postponed last month because of insecurity, and a first-round vote is now set for July. Moïse has not publicly commented on her registration, but wrote on X last week that “Haiti will rise again on its own two feet, because politics needs to be done differently.”
stories.why: A first vote in a decade would be a key step toward restoring an elected government in a country where armed gangs control much of the capital. Moïse’s candidacy brings the unresolved 2021 assassination back into the campaign — but the July date still depends on security.

stories.headline: Mirra Andreeva, 19, beats Elina Svitolina to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set
stories.deck: Russia’s Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Indian Wells, California, on Sunday to win the WTA Finals, the event’s youngest champion in 22 years.
stories.summary: Russia’s Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Indian Wells, California, on Sunday to win the WTA Finals, the event’s youngest champion in 22 years. The French Open champion did not drop a set all week and lost only 26 games in five matches, the BBC reported. She rises to No. 2 in the world, 293 points behind Elena Rybakina going into 2027. The players did not shake hands after the match, Al Jazeera noted; Ukrainian players have declined to shake hands with Russian and Belarusian opponents since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion, in line with their federation’s policy. Andreeva also won a custom purple Mercedes — though, at 19, she said she still needs a driver’s licence.
stories.why: Andreeva’s dominance makes her a clear challenger for No. 1 next season. The final was also another reminder of how the war in Ukraine still shapes the women’s tour.
